result.statement: If the universal interval bound with constant C is proved in every dimension only for independent smooth compactly supported cap-one inputs and matrices having at least three eigenvalues of absolute value strictly greater than one, then the full owner target for arbitrary rough/unbounded cap-one product laws and threshold abs(lambda)>=1 follows with exactly the same C. The same C also extends to arbitrary deterministic affine perturbations X^TAX+b^TX+c via one far-translated auxiliary cap-one coordinate. Arbitrary deterministic coordinate translations are therefore zero-cost. Continuity is not transferred by the limiting argument.

proof_components.cap_preserving_compactification: f_R=f 1_[−R,R]+1_[R+1,R+1+delta_R], delta_R=P(|X|>R); TV<=delta_R and density cap remains <=1
proof_components.product_transfer: product TV <= sum marginal TV and measurable pushforwards contract TV
proof_components.strict_margin: apply restricted theorem to (1+eta)A and send eta down to zero
proof_components.affine_homogenization: B_T=[[(1+||b||/T)A,b/(2T)],[b^T/(2T),0]], Y_T=T+U; off-diagonal norm ||b||/(2T), Weyl preserves three strict large eigenvalues, and the homogeneous output converges a.s. to X^TAX+b^TX with no moment use
proof_components.smoothing: mollify compact cap-one marginals; convolution preserves the cap, mass and compact support and converges in L1

partner_result_applied.actual_inequality: P(Q in I) <= (4+2 log 8)|I| + sum_{j=1}^4 P(|X_j|>R), hence ||p_Q||_infinity <=4+2 log 8=8.158883083359672... after R->infinity
